title: User-grain portfolio and mini-feature thesis — field notes
content:
TL;DR:
A compact synthesis of recent field calls (8 enterprise customers, mix of hosted & dedicated) that centers on three recurring themes: (1) unpredictable per-token cost spikes when prompt lengths vary, (2) kv-prefix cache confusion (customers misunderstanding what is cached), and (3) rollout fragility when model variants are swapped under heavy traffic.

Purpose / method:
- Quick aggregation from CS call notes, three recorded demos, and the internal latency-quirk tickets.
- Prioritized by perceived customer impact (revenue/ops pain) + ease of transit to a small experiment.
- This doc = working deck for a 30m sync with ENG + PRODUCT next Wed.

Top hypotheses (ranked):
1) Cost volatility is driving most "we want predictability" asks. Customers run mixed-length pipelines (summarization + follow-ups) and budgeting tools are blind to distribution tails. Long tail => surprise billing.
2) KV caching mental model mismatch: customers assume prefix caching will make per-user conversations cheap; but TTLs, model pinning, and cross-variant compatibility create unexpected cache misses.
3) Canary+fallback race: when we flip to lighter-weight quantized variants for cost, some customers see higher error rates in rare edge prompts; automated fallback is sometimes too slow or opaque.

Feature sketchlets (mini features that could move the needle quickly):
A) "Cost-slice" dashboard: show token distribution percentiles (p50/p90/p99) per route + simulated cost under alternative batching/quantization profiles. Low-dev: surface existing analytics, add percentiles and a slider. Owner: Product-hosted-api. Linked ticket: JIRA-CS-8123.

B) "KV-clarifier" UX: inline note in Console for model-variant combos that are cache-compatible + a simple diagnostic endpoint that returns a cache-hit probability for a given prefix. Minimal runtime hook + Console flag. West coast customer asked for this specifically (call 2026-03-30).

C) Canary visualization & auto-rollback policy: expose real-time mismatch rate and allow setting a lightweight rollback threshold (e.g., mismatch > 1% for 5m). Can be gated behind Dedicated customers first. Engineering spike estimate: 2w.

Low-effort experiments (0–2 week):
- Add p90/p99 token-length telemetry to existing route metrics (instrumentation only).
- Console tweak: show last-5 cache-hit-rate per customer; surface probable causes (variant mismatch, TTL).
- Run an internal "billing-sim" on 10 customers to model spike exposure.

Customer quotes (raw snippets):
- "We budgeted for 60M tokens and then the summarizer ran a 12k prompt and ate the month." — enterprise-friend
- "We thought caching would just happen per conversation. Turns out we lost a bunch of hits when you changed the variant." — platform-eng@customer
- "Can we be alerted when a rollout causes a conv-quality delta? Not just errors but content drift." — SRE lead, fintech

Metrics to watch if we ship A/Bs:
- Per-route token-length percentiles (p50/p90/p99), per-customer spend variance
- KV cache hit-rate delta pre/post model swap
- Canary mismatch rate and rollback frequency

Tradeoffs / risks:
- Adding more telemetry increases cost and storage; need to TTL metrics aggressively.
- Exposing cache probabilities creates expectations; if we surface a low probability and nothing changes, customer anger.
- Auto rollback might hide upstream regressions if thresholds are too loose.

Questions / open items (notes to self):
- How intrusive is adding a cache-hit-prob endpoint to the runtime? (Ping SRE/serving-runtime).
- Can we model billing spikes with synthetic workload generator? (Spike team? release-engineering?)
- Is a dedicated console flag for "experimental rollback" okay from compliance perspective for Private customers? (Ask security/compliance).

Next steps (this week):
1) Sync w/ Product-hosted-api on Cost-slice MVP scope — Asha + Priya (Mon).
2) Engineering triage: ask serving-runtime for hit-prob hook feasibility — Miguel (Tue).
3) Run quick billing-sim on 5 pilot customers (internal only) and bring results to Wed sync.

Appendix — short technical notes:
- TTL interaction: if model variant changes, cached KV entries may be invalidated implicitly by model id mismatch; customers often don't realize variant=quantized vs base changes cache semantics.
- Batching effect: longer prompts increase batching opportunities but also increase tail latency; some customers disable batching for latency-sensitive lanes, increasing unit cost.

Raw call log pointers:
- /recordings/2026-03-30-demo-fintech.mp3 (private)
- /call-notes/2026-03-25-customer-x.md

TODO/Risks: add a short one-pager for execs showing projected $ impact of token spikes (estimate needed).

---
Staccato notes (brain dump):
- consider a "budget guardrail" product: set p99 token cap per route -> soft block + notify.
- explore making cache compatibility visible in model catalog ("compatible-with-cache" badge).
- check if any Dedicated contracts disallow auto-rollback without customer opt-in.

End of doc — rough, conversational, intended for fast iteration.
